purpose: A musician controlling SMC Solo over USB/peripheral User MIDI must retain correct NoteOn/NoteOff fail-safe behavior if the independent direct BLE central disconnects and the separate host queue saturates.
design: Extend registered production-C source-extraction regression for host Solo release-loss while direct BLE central is offline. Vary host FIFO wrap, zero-velocity NoteOn vs NoteOff, owned channel-16 vs foreign channel-3 release and optional reconnect. Keep all production source unchanged. A deliberately broken main-loop guard requiring BLE up must fail.
expected_observable_user_effect: USB SMC Solo remains usable without direct BLE; a dropped accepted host release clears held Solo, foreign MIDI does not, and new presses work after reconnect. This is intended behavior protected by tests, not measured device reliability.

native_evidence.environment: container Linux x86_64; Python 3.13.5; GCC 14.2.0; Clang 17 (compiler modes plain, UBSan, ASan+UBSan)

deliberately_broken_negative.failed_at: owned lost USB NoteOff fails safe offline; foreign key-up does not

native_evidence.execution_note: Several aggregate driver invocations reached their tool-level time limit; completed individual logs were retained, missing cases executed on later invocations, and all 18 expected outcomes verified. No aggregate timeout itself was recorded as a pass.
